gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Stentiga spreads its letters wide, with crossbars as heavy as the stems and no thin strokes anywhere. Noto Sans Wancho counters with a hulking lowercase, pressed down like thick chalk, and that sturdy weight is the pair's best asset.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-warang-: Stentiga is luxurious and spread out, with no hairlines at all.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-yi: Pencil-line consistency, refined and wide. Noto Sans Yi follows with a deep-bodied lowercase and open rounds, so a long page of text moves along without snagging.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-zanabaz: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square stands tall and crisp.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-traditional-: Noto Traditional Nushu writes like a broad-nibbed pen, its bowls filling the line and never curling shut. Beside it, Stentiga looks bent from a single length of wire, so the two feel like pen and wire.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-onest: Onest reads gently, with short ascenders over big bowls.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-open-sans: Open Sans reads smoothly, with no clogged curves and a bulky lowercase that fills the line. And Stentiga, drawn like wire, spreads its letters wide above it, so the heading feels light against that heavier body.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-orienta: Spread-out and pipe-cleaner thin, Stentiga looks refined while Orienta keeps its counters open like a cut reed. One shows off; the other reads.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-oxygen: Refined, with crossbars the same bar thickness as the stems, Stentiga sets a spread-out rhythm. Oxygen follows with curves that never close and a lowercase nearly matching its capitals, so the heading and text sit close in height.
